title: Confirmed numbered EGA corrections and proof comparisons
as_he_states: Preserve the locality, differential-sign, integral-closure and completion-formula checks outside the narrow19.4.6 question.
plausible_today: Each is a separate edition-specific check; a sign convention is not a false theorem, and a suggested weakening is not an already established erratum.
state_of_art: Three exact checks are now complete. Printed0.16.1.9 p24 assumes noetherianity; its dimension equality extends without it because the faithful finite-module determinant trick makes B/Ann_B(M) integral over A/Ann_A(M), and integral extensions preserve dimension. Printed0.19.8.3 pp110–111 claims uniqueness among homomorphisms from a prime local ring: locality is essential, since every Z_(p) maps nonlocally to Q. Printed0.20.4.13(iv) p127 has the integral-closure hypothesis; localization gives Omega_B/A tensor Frac(B)=Omega_Frac(B)/Frac(A)=0 for an algebraic separable fraction extension, without integral closure. The0.20.4.6 sign is a convention requiring coherent propagation. The19.4.6–7 simplification proposals are not independently certified. Original EGAIII1,4.3.6 printedp133, has the alleged false equality. For A=Q[x,y]_(x,y), the prime (y−(exp(x)−1)) in Ahat contracts to0 and survives localization by A minus0, so Frac(A) tensor_A Ahat is not a field. The desired analytically-integral implies unibranch argument nevertheless works with the natural inclusion into Frac(Ahat). Full details are in proof_notes.md §11. The later published errata confirm the first three corrections and record the sign change, subject to the printed old/new-label transposition just described. Exact later errata: EGA IV4 Liste 3 de corrections, IV nos.6,9,12–14, printed pp.347–348 (1967). No.6 removes noetherianity from 0.16.1.9; no.9 inserts local in 0.19.8.3/4; nos.12–13 change the differential convention; no.14 removes integral closure in 0.20.4.13(iv) and supplies a denominator-clearing argument. The first p1/p2 instruction in no.12 itself has old/new labels reversed relative to the original p.125; its explicit tensor formula and no.13 determine the intended change. The 19.4.6–7 suggested proof simplifications remain separate bounded verification questions. The III4.3.6 equality is now verified false in the original print, while its conclusion is independently recovered using the natural injection.

source_cues.verbatim:
\uline{Proposition 7.4}

Let g:   X $\to$ S be a flat proper morphism, let s $\in$ S let us
put n = dim X$_s$ and let us suppose that the dimension of the set of
points of X$_s$ where X$_s$ is not separable over k(s) is  $<$ n.  (\uline{for
example}  X$_s$   separable).  Then there exists an open neighborhood
U of s and an \'etale finite, surjective morphism S1---> U such that
X \quad x$_S$ \quad S1 \quad admits a section over S1 .  If k(s) is infinite we
may take for S$^1$ a closed subscheme of \uline{X\ \ U}.*  Let us assume to
start with that k(s) is infinite.

We proceed by induction on n, the case n = 0 being trivial.
Indeed in that case there exists an open neighbourhood U of s such
that X|U itself is \'etale, finite and surjective above U as we see
by immediate cross references.  If n $>$ 0, we apply 7.3 for the
``separable'' property which allows us to replace X by a ``hyperplane
section'' $\underline{Y}$ having the same properties up to this that n is
replaced by n-1.  If k(s) is not assumed infinite we begin by
making an \'etale base change, it works.

\margin{* unclear, ask a.g.}

\uline{Remark 7.5}

In particular if $X$ is projective and separable over $S$ it
admits locally over $S$ étale multisections.  But we note that we
can give examples with $X$ proper and smooth (but non-projective) $S$,
where the same conclusion fails.  Of course, the projective
assumption cannot be weakened in general to an assumption of
quasi-projectiveness as we see for example by taking $X$ étale non-%
finite over $S$ ......

pre_origin_audit_record.plausible_today: Use finite étale component torsors and split reductive SO torsors in the smooth cases; in odd rank first a finite flat μ2 torsor.
pre_origin_audit_record.state_of_art: As of19November2026. Conrad2014 C.1.5, printed305–308, proves the smoothness criterion and explains O_(2m+1)=μ2×SO′ and the even-rank component distinction. The draft’s reduction through a μ2 torsor is valid in its odd-rank paragraph, not as an all-rank assertion. SGA3 XXIV4.2.3 proves that a torsor under a split reductive group over a semilocal base is trivialized by a finite étale surjective cover. Apply this to the split special orthogonal factor after the finite component torsor; in odd rank first use the finite locally free μ2 torsor. Finite presentation spreads the resulting cover and isometry from a local base to a Zariski neighborhood. Thus the asserted Zariski-local finite étale trivialization in the smooth cases, and finite flat trivialization in general, are established. This is not a theorem about arbitrary smooth groups.
pre_origin_audit_record.why_open: The author references a theorem not reproduced and asks about the exceptional case.
pre_origin_audit_record.worth: The exact finite-cover theorem is now identified; no unrestricted étale assertion remains.
